newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION - Two Pumas improve their test chances.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION - Two Pumas improve their test chances.

text.p: NEW PLYMOUTH, June 25 - Two players enhanced their test chances yesterday though Argentina failed yet again to provide any evidence of their rugby education in New Zealand, NZPA reports.
Their 10-26 loss to Taranaki exposed the flaws that featured in their record 8-93 first-test defeat last Saturday and gave their shaky position in the international pecking order a further jolt.
A dismal tour of New Zealand will have done their efforts to obtain more international fixtures against teams like South Africa, Australia and New Zealand no favour.
Their present campaign for a place or two in the Super 12 has also been jeopardised by their poor results.

With only the second test on Saturday remaining in their five-game tour, the tourists have won just one match -- a 42-10 victory over a second and third division combination from Nelson Bays and Marlborough. They lost the Athletic Park test, 17-39 to the New Zealand Maori and to Taranaki at Rugby Park, New Plymouth, yesterday by four- tries-to-one.
For a team rated in the world's top eight, Argentina were at least expected to compete in the test. Nothing they've done on the field yet has pointed in that direction.
The only bright bits to their disorganised and visionless performance yesterday were Diego Albanese and Pablo Bouza, and Albanese's try from a blindside attack that started 60 metres away.
"I think the number 11 and number eight did well today," Pumas coach Jose Imhoff said of left wing Albanese and loose forward Bouza.

Albanese showed some penetration and sound rugby sense with a few determined runs. When halfback Christian Barrea raced around the blindside of a scrum in the 26th minute, Albanese latched on to the attack, exchanged passes twice with Barrea
before sprinting away clear for a converted try.
It was the only time the Pumas led in heavy conditions made worse by torrential rain.
Albanese could be a serious challenger for the right wing's berth held by Tomas Solari when the second test side is named either this afternoon or tomorrow.
Solari failed to hold Tana Umaga down at Athletic Park.

Bouza, bracketed in last Saturday's test side with Christian Viel until kickoff, was impressive on defence and one of the two Argentine forwards, the other being flanker Roberto Travaglini, who tried hard to start a forward momentum.
"I thought we were going okay until halftime and then we tried to keep the ball tight instead of having a go and moving it wide," Pumas coach Jose Imhoff said.

Alex Wyllie, the team's technical adviser and a former All Black coach, said the most disappointing part of the disorganised Pumas game was their inability to apply what they had practised and talked about.

"They had opportunities to score points but individuals seemed to take it on their own and do their own things. It's just the way they are. They have to learn that if things don't work for the first few minutes or the first 30 minutes they've
got to keep going as a team," Wyllie said.

The Pumas sacrificed a number of kickable penalties for scrums or quick taps, and even kicked for touch with the hope of winning the ensuing lineout and then attacking the line. Nothing worked in the face of a strong Taranaki defence, but their own errors also contributed much to their inablity to penetrate.
Taranaki, under new coach Jed Rowlands, fielded seven newcomers and were not in vintage form.
But they played common-sense rugby in the difficult conditions, kept the ball away from the reputed Pumas pack as much as possible, used their speed effectively and tackled efficiently.

Their pack had enough experience in Kevin Barrett, Andrew and Gordon Slater, Scott Lines and Shane McDonald. Darryl Fale would have given the touring team some valuable lessons about a flanker's role if they had watched him closely.
In the backs, Richard Jarman and Mark Urwin provided opportunities for the outside backs and Jason Holland and Mark Robinson caused plenty of worries for the Pumas defence.
Second half tries by wingers Lea Potaufa and Filipo Toala were testimony of Taranaki's willingness to play wide and stretch the opposition defence.

Robinson scored the match's first try in the eight minute and Barrett, who set up Toala's five-pointer in the 79th minute, scored the second in the 33rd minute, which gave the home side a 14-10 halftime cushion.
